correctness.rationale: The source lower bound gives depth at least \(n+1\). For the upper bound, a positive legal cylinder beginning \(ab\) lies in \(L\cap a^2L\) because left multiplication by \(a^{-2}\) changes only the initial legal transition to \(a^{-1}\to b\). Measure-class preservation makes every translated consecutive intersection positive. Translating a positive legal cylinder beginning with \(b\) by \(a^{2n+2}\) gives a positive subset of \(a^{2n+2}L\cap B_n\). Thus an \(n+1\)-chain exists. For \(n=0\), \(L\cap[a^2]\) is empty because \(P(a,a)=0\), so the same equality holds.

value.rationale: The sets \(B_n\) are the canonical witnesses used to separate chaining from bounded chaining in the source. Their exact minimum chain depth is therefore a motivated invariant of the flagship example, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The equality gives the sharp quantitative growth hidden behind the qualitative non-boundedness argument and provides a natural benchmark for future quantitative versions of the property.
